analysis:
Documentation-only PR touching docs/provider/direct-mode.md and docs/reference/configuration.md; no executable code, auth, crypto or protocol source is changed, so no concrete security regression is identifiable from the supplied evidence.

direct-mode.md (head lines 340-342): the new text says served-speed records now carry a local-API origin marker and a tensor-assistant flag, and that plans for serving through Darkbloom ignore local records. This is a values-only telemetry file (~/.darkbloom/cluster/served-speed.json) with no prompt, output or client identity, so it does not touch A-001. The claim that Darkbloom-served plans ignore local records is a documented control that I could not verify, because the implementing source (DistributedPairTelemetryRecorder) is not in the batch.

configuration.md changes cluster public-model/approval semantics. resource_policy_sha256 now includes the tensor-assistant fields (depth, inventory SHA, verification, evidence hash) when the build declares an assistant public. The tensor_parallel schedule-1 qualification cites a new report, docs/reports/2026-11-05-qwen27-public-assistant.md. The mtp_mode text now lets a cluster served through Darkbloom use a build-declared public assistant (previously never). The tensorAssistantServesLocally validation relaxes from refusing any assistant beside nativeMember to refusing all but the exact build-declared public policy. This widens what the coordinator-facing pair may advertise and run, with a bilaterally bound policy hash and an evidence hash. Relevant threat areas are T-007 (manipulated outputs, not cryptographically provable), T-054 and T-056 (overclaiming qualification or correctness). The text correctly states that the exact build-declared policy is required and that the leader rejects a mismatched approval before stopping any part. The underlying enforcement code (ClusterConfiguration.validate, ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant) and the evidence report's content are not supplied. Whether that relaxation is implemented as documented, and whether the evidence supports public serving, needs source-level review when the code change is available. The documentation does not claim runtime secrecy or correctness beyond the evidence, consistent with T-056.

T-041 (prefix cache) is not affected.
